document.title: National Intelligence Daily (NID 96-0229CX)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Top Secret] Four days after the Taliban took Kabul, the CIA notes the Taliban closed camps tied to Hekmatyar, Sayyaf and Jamaat-i-Islami but not those associated with bin Laden, Hizb-i-Islami (Khalis), Jamiat-Ulema-i-Islam and Harakat ul-Ansar, including HUA's main camp in Khowst.

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
persons.role: Patron of militant training camps in Afghanistan that the Taliban had not closed

mentions.quote: Taliban has not closed other camps associated with Usama bin Ladin, Hizbi Islami (Khalis), Pakistan's Jamiat-Ulema-i-Islam, and Harakat ul-Ansar

persons.name: Gulbuddin Hikmatyar
persons.role: Factional leader whose associated militant training camps were closed by the Taliban

mentions.quote: has closed militant training camps associated with Hikmatyar, factional leader Sayyaf, and Pakistan's Jamaat-i-Islami

persons.name: Sayyaf
persons.role: Afghan factional leader whose associated training camps were closed by the Taliban

mentions.quote: camps associated with Hikmatyar, factional leader Sayyaf, and Pakistan's Jamaat-i-Islami

persons.name: Burhanuddin Rabbani
persons.role: Deposed President of Afghanistan, supported by India

mentions.quote: India probably will continue to support deposed President Rabbani

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Captured Kabul in Sept 1996; mixed record on terrorism, closing some camps while tolerating others; predominantly Pashtun.

organizations.name: Hizb-i Islami (Hikmatyar)
organizations.notes: Implied by reference to camps associated with Hikmatyar, which the Taliban closed.

organizations.name: Harakat ul-Ansar
organizations.notes: Its main training camp in Khowst was not closed by the Taliban.

organizations.name: Jamiat-Ulema-i-Islam
organizations.notes: Associated camps not closed by the Taliban.

organizations.name: Jamaat-i-Islami
organizations.notes: Associated militant training camps closed by the Taliban.

organizations.name: Pakistan government
organizations.notes: Appears ready to recognize the Taliban; some Taliban believe the US funnels aid via Pakistani authorities.

organizations.name: United Nations
organizations.notes: Peace process in which the Taliban showed scant interest.

events.description: CIA assessment of the impact of the Taliban victory in Kabul: consolidation, a mixed record on terrorism, regional reactions.
Taliban take Kabul and depose President Rabbani.
Taliban victory in Kabul; deposed Rabbani; Taliban consolidating rule.
Taliban closed militant training camps associated with Hikmatyar, Sayyaf, and Jamaat-i-Islami while leaving bin Ladin, Khalis, JUI and HUA camps open.

key_claims: The Taliban tolerated some terrorist groups while closing others.
Taliban closed camps linked to Hikmatyar, Sayyaf and Pakistan's Jamaat-i-Islami but not those linked to bin Ladin, Khalis, JUI or HUA.
HUA's main training camp in Khowst remained open under Taliban rule.
Pakistan alone among neighbors seemed ready to recognize the Taliban, but would go slowly.
Some Taliban officials believe the US has funneled assistance to them through Pakistani authorities.
The Taliban were expected to face ethnic minority resistance in the north.
